title: Assurance partnerships: handoff sprint brief
content:
Purpose:
This brief outlines a 4-week cross-functional sprint to formalize operational handoffs, instrument measurable service-level objectives (service-level objectives / SLOs), and create an ‘assurance partnership’ checklist between feature teams and SRE. The goal is a repeatable handoff that minimizes release risk, clarifies SLO ownership, and leaves teams with runnable runbooks and dashboards.

Context and why now:
- Multiple recent rollouts exposed gaps: inconsistent error-budget accounting, missing escalation playbooks, and feature teams shipping without telemetry for important user journeys.
- Leadership asked for a lightweight, reproducible handoff pattern that reduces TOIL on oncall and enforces minimal observability/rollback guardrails.
- This sprint pilot will be applied to two upcoming launches (Search v5 and Embeddings API v2) as the first proof points.

Sprint goals (measurable):
- Define and agree SLO candidates for the pilot services (latency P50/P95 targets, request success rate).
- Produce a validated handoff checklist and a template runbook for feature teams that includes rollback criteria and postmortem triggers.
- Build and publish baseline dashboards and alert rules for the SRE console; ensure dashboards show production baseline, burn rate, and a regression watchlist.
- Demo the handoff and gather feedback from product/infra by end of week 4.

Success metrics (acceptance criteria):
- Both pilot services have SLOs configured in the SLO registry and linked to alerts (score = configured).
- Automated dashboard ingestion of key metrics (latency histogram, error counts, throughput) within 24 hours of deployment in the staging-to-prod pipeline.
- Runbook acceptance: feature team + oncall sign-off that the runbook covers 90% of critical recovery flows.
- <10% increase in P1 noise from new alerts after tuning.

Scope (what is in/out):
In scope:
- SLO definition (candidate metrics and targets) for pilot services.
- Runbook template, escalation matrix, and rollback criteria.
- Basic dashboards and alert rules (no full long-term retention/coverage).
- Lightweight CI checks for telemetry presence in PRs for the pilot teams.

Out of scope:
- Full org-wide SLO cataloging.
- Long-term observability retention policy changes.
- Rewriting existing oncall runbooks unrelated to the pilots.

Stakeholders and roles:
- Product owners: Lina Rodriguez (Search v5), Dev Patel (Embeddings API v2) — fund and validate user impact thresholds.
- Feature engineers: respective service leads — implement instrumentation and runbook drafts.
- SRE leads: Maya Thompson (program lead), Owen Michaels (oncall readiness) — enforce reliability gates, runbook templates, and alerting.
- Observability: Priya Chang — dashboard / metric ingestion owner.
- Security/Compliance: consult as needed for private-deploy features.

Phases & week-by-week plan:
Week 0 (pre-sprint prep, 3 days):
- Alignment sync: program lead + product + feature leads. Create initial SLO candidates and minimal telemetry checklist. (Jira OPS-8421 created)
- Create repo templates: runbook-md, dashboard-json template, PR telemetry checklist.

Week 1 (measure):
- Engineers add traceable metric names and tags to key code paths; expose latency histograms and success counters.
- Observability team pairs to validate metrics collection in staging.
- Draft SLOs: propose baseline targets (P50, P95 latency, request success rate) and document rationale.

Week 2 (protect):
- SRE authors initial alert rules based on candidate SLO burn rates and hard thresholds.
- Runbook first draft: top 5 failure modes, quick rollback steps, key dashboards, and postmortem triggers.
- Feature teams add CI check so PRs failing to register required metrics block merge.

Week 3 (tune):
- Oncall simulation: run a 2-hour war room exercise with injected failures to test runbook completeness and alert fidelity.
- Tune alert noise, adjust thresholds, fix gaps exposed by simulations.

Week 4 (formalize + handoff):
- Finalize SLOs and publish to SLO registry.
- SRE + feature team sign-off on runbook and dashboards.
- Demo for stakeholders and capture feedback for follow-up backlog items.

Handoff protocol (template):
- Pre-merge checklist (feature owner responsibility): metrics instrumented (histogram, counter), A/B gating plan, intended SLO candidate, rollout cadence.
- Pre-launch checklist (joint): staging-to-prod telemetry validated, runbook reviewed by oncall, alerting rule exists and is tested, rollback automation verified (if available).
- Launch day play: designate runbook owner, have SRE observer on go/no-go call, monitor burn-rate dashboard first 2 hours, prepare rapid rollback threshold.
- Post-launch Q48: retrospective focused on observed SLO deltas and alert behavior; log follow-up tasks.

Runbook minimum contents (to be templated):
- Service summary and owners (pager, slack, escalation list).
- Symptoms and detection (what alerts/fire conditions mean).
- Immediate mitigation steps (3 bullet actions to stabilize).
- Rollback procedure with criteria and commands.
- Postmortem trigger rules and where to file.

Risk matrix (top 4 risks and mitigations):
- Risk: Missing metrics due to library mismatch. Mitigation: Pre-merge binary check + observability pair review.
- Risk: Alert overload after launch. Mitigation: Simulated failure tuning + threshold ramping policy.
- Risk: Ownership ambiguity for rollbacks. Mitigation: Named runbook owner and go/no-go authority established before launch.
- Risk: Performance regressions post-shipping. Mitigation: Canary rollout with canary-specific SLO burn tracking and automated rollback on spike.

Telemetry & dashboards checklist:
- Latency histograms (P50/P95) split by critical route and traffic class.
- Success/error counters aggregated to a 1m resolution.
- Burn-rate panel for configured SLOs + past-week baseline.
- Regression watchlist: new metric deltas highlighted.

Communication and cadence:
- Daily 30m standup Mon–Fri during sprint with program lead + feature leads + observability.
- Weekly stakeholder review (30m) to surface blockers and decisions.
- Launch day war-room (as needed) with 1:1 SRE liaison pinned.

Deliverables and artifacts (what we will publish):
- SLO registry entries for both pilots (with rationale and targets).
- Runbook templates checked into infra/runbooks/<service>.md.
- Dashboard JSONs in observability/dashboards/<service>.json.
- Post-sprint retro doc capturing lessons and next steps.

Rollout criteria and quality gates:
- Telemetry gate: CI validated telemetry in >95% of staged requests.
- Alert gate: No more than 2 high-priority false positives during simulation.
- Ownership gate: Named oncall and runbook owner with pager assignments verified.

Open questions and decisions needed this sprint:
- What are firm SLO targets for Embeddings API v2 given the expected request shape? (Product input required)
- Do we require automated rollback for both pilots or only for latency-sensitive endpoints?
- Which retention tier will the dashboards use in the long term — short-term plan acceptable, but policy owners should weigh in.

Immediate next steps (owner):
- Maya: schedule alignment sync and create OPS-8421 subtasks (today).
- Dev: sketch SLO candidate numbers and post in the sprint doc (by EOD).
- Priya: prepare a dashboard skeleton and verify instrumentation naming (by Day 2).

Appendix: quick checklist for feature teams before handoff:
- Metric names follow telemetry naming conventions.
- Histogram + counter present for each critical path.
- SLO candidate documented with business impact rationale.
- Runbook draft exists and a reviewer assigned.
- CI telemetry check added to PR templates.

Notes to self / running log (work-in-progress):
- Keep checklist intentionally small: aim for the ‘minimum viable assurance’ to avoid blocking teams.
- Capture learnings in a short retro and convert to a lightweight internal FAQ for repeatability.
- After 2 pilots, evaluate whether to make this sprint checklist mandatory for major launches.

End of brief.
